newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Hasan said to deny tender offer for Astra.
newsitem.headline: Hasan said to deny tender offer for Astra.

text.p: A group to which Indonesia's President Suharto is linked has denied it will make a general offer for shares in Astra International, but is willing to buy stock at market prices, Bisnis Indonesia reported on Thursday.

The newspaper quoted Nusamba group commissioner Muhamad "Bob" Hasan as saying in an interview that the venture will not buy into Astra, the country's largest vehicle manufacturer, if the share price was too high.
Hasan was not immediately available for comment.
He said Nusamba was willing to consider offers from existing shareholders but would not make a tender offer itself.
Newspapers had reported earlier this week that Nusamba could make a general offer for Astra at between 4,100-4,200 rupiah per share.
The reports led to a brief surge in the share price, to 4,150 rupiah early on Monday, but they later slipped back.
On Thursday, Astra was trading at 3,900 rupiah in morning trade, down 25.
Hasan declined to say if any shareholders had offered to sell their holdings. "It is my company secret. I cannot let you know," he said, according to the newspaper report.
Nusamba is 80 percent owned by three foundations headed by Suharto. Hasan, a close associate of Suharto, and the president's eldest son Sigit Harjojudanto own 10 percent each.

Astra shares had soared last month on newspaper reports that a takeover bid could be in progress but tapered off after tobacco tycoon Putera Sampoerna announced he had bought a 9.81 percent stake in the firm.
His PT Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna cigarette company then announced that a subsidiary had bought an additional 2.85 percent stake in Astra, giving Putera Sampoerna effectively the largest shareholding.
Newspapers at the time said Sampoerna might sell his stake to Nusamba, which Hasan denied.
Astra is a widely-held company and brokers have said an 18-20 percent stake may be sufficient to gain a controlling interest.
Japan's Toyota Motor Co holds an 8.26 percent stake.
